note: How the game feeds its sound (src/audio/index.js, src/audio/game-state.js, src/world/sound-near.js; docs 17 and 25). updateHz: how often the sound state is built and the ambience updated (doc 17: 10 Hz). near: what is close to the camera target, sampled every nearEveryS seconds over a circle of radiusM (doc 17: within 12 m), cell by cell (the water summary's half-meter cells, the growth grid's one-meter cells), each cell weighted by closeness (1 at the center, falloff at the edge). Water kinds come from the water summary's classes: still is pond water, slow and running are streams. Ponds count by their share of the circle; streams are thin, so slow and running count by how close the nearest stream cell is: full within streamFullM, easing to none at radiusM. Cells beyond the summary are open sea; the sea counts toward nearWater for the rain on open water, but not toward the pond lap. fullAt is the share of weighted points that counts as fully near (so a pond filling a third of the circle already sounds like a pond). Pads and reeds count plants within plantReachM of each point, each species at its weight in pads and reeds (lilies make pads; reeds, and irises at half, make reeds); the rush cover counts as reeds at rushWeight. grass: the grass cover (0..255) that counts as full grass. gust: the wind's gusts, which the weather does not keep, made here on a seeded rhythm: a gust comes every everyS seconds (shorter as wind rises, divided by everyWindScale plus the wind), rises to a peak between peak[0] and peak[1] scaled up by the wind, lasts holdS, and the level follows its target at followPerS. frost (doc 25): winter mornings are frosty until the sun burns it off. frost = the winter weight, times a curve of hours from sunrise (byHourFromSunrise, flat past the ends), times 1 - cloudCut * cloud, and none while it rains. afterRainH: game hours of drips after rain stops (doc 25 asks for one to two). mobile: a phone is a coarse pointer with a short screen side under phoneMaxSidePx (the audio check page uses the same rule). seed: the sub-seed for this system's streams.
